_README: WHICH INSTRUMENT each printed staff of each printed system carries, for pdf pages 1-4 of this edition. This is what the ordinal join is wrong about, and nothing machine-readable in the repo held it.
_provenance:
TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES THAT AGREE, and neither is a reading of the same raster the join is made from.
  (1) HAND-READ: benchmarks/omr-cleanup-count-2026-09/printed-staves.json, whose per-system counts and prose notes ('system 2 suppresses Oboi, Trombe and Timpani'; 'system 1 suppresses Timpani and SPLITS the bottom staff; system 2 keeps Timpani and condenses it again') were transcribed from the hand-verified works.json rows.
  (2) OCR: the margin labels the page itself prints, read by probe/margin_label_reach.py (out/margin-label-reach.log, 50 labels over 75 staves). The opening system reads 12 of 12 -- Flauti, Oboi, Clarinetti, Fagotti, Corni, Trombe, Timpani, Violino I, Violino II, Viola, Violoncello, Basso -- which is where `full` below comes from; and page 3's 8-stave system reads Fl./Cl./Fag./Cor., NO Ob., which is source (2) confirming source (1)'s suppression list on the one system that matters most.
_why_two_sources: CLAUDE.md's standing hazard: an arbiter read off the same raster as the reading it arbitrates falls silent exactly where it is needed. Source (1) is a human on the print and cannot. Source (2) can -- and it is used only as CORROBORATION of (1), never alone. Where they disagreed, nothing would be written here; they do not.
_not_established: The lineup is named ONLY for pdf pages 1-4 of ONE edition of ONE movement. Nothing here is a claim about page 5 onward, about another Litolff plate, or about any other publisher.
